intro_html: Yes, root beer, and yes, it works. Zero-sugar soda and sugar-free barbecue sauce keep this pulled pork lean while the slow cooker turns tenderloin into fork-tender shreds. It goes over potatoes with a little cabbage on the side, runs around $4.16 a serving (at everyday cost), and packs 59 grams of protein across 14 bowls.
cost_closing_html: About $4.16 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Each bowl delivers 59 grams of protein and 560 calories, with just 9 grams of fat per serving.
upsell_html: A fun little trick that turns cheap soda and lean pork into a dinner people ask about. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: Sugar-free barbecue sauce cuts the sugar without cutting flavor. Grab the sugar-free bottle and nobody will know the difference.
Zero-sugar soda is often cheaper by the store brand. Buy the generic diet soda instead of the name brand for the same result.
Green cabbage is one of the cheapest vegetables per pound all year. Buy a whole head of cabbage and use it across several meals.
make_it: Add the pork tenderloin, sliced onion, and garlic to the slow cooker.
Pour in the zero-sugar soda and half the barbecue sauce.
Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours until the pork pulls apart easily.
Shred the pork, drain off most of the liquid, and stir in the rest of the barbecue sauce.
Roast or boil the potatoes until fork tender.
Pile the pulled pork over the potatoes and top with the shredded cabbage for crunch.
